samples.summary: Second, divergent definition of "the blockquote prefix" in the same package: `toggleQuote`'s `QUOTE_RE = /^\s*>\s?/` vs the new `list-commands.ts` `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` (and `checkbox-input.ts`'s `BARE_BOX_RE`).
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/commands.ts:278 `const QUOTE_RE = /^\s*>\s?/;` used at :293/:297 to detect and strip the quote for the Quote toolbar button, while packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:45 now defines a stricter, depth-aware prefix and packages/notes/src/view/checkbox-input.ts:9 a third variant. Concretely: on `\t> quoted` or `    > quoted` the Quote button happily strips the marker (its regex matches after any whitespace), whereas the list buttons now deliberately refuse those same lines via `hasUnpeeledQuote` (list-commands.ts:111). Same-looking prefix, three notions of it — the two will drift the next time either is touched, and the toolbar's behaviour on those lines is already inconsistent (Quote acts, Bullet/Indent silently no-op). Fix belongs on the new code: share one exported prefix helper.

samples.summary: Lines that merely *look* quoted — e.g. shell-prompt or e-mail-quote lines inside a fenced code block — were incidentally protected by the removed `quoted` bail-out and are now rewritten by the list toggles.
samples.evidence: Before this change `replacePrefixes` skipped any line matching `/^\s*>/` (old `ParsedLine.quoted`), so a selection spanning a fence whose body contains `> npm run build` left that line untouched. Now `parseLine` peels `> ` as a real blockquote and `replacePrefixes` (packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:256) rewrites the prefix, so `toggleBulletList` turns fenced content `> npm run build` into `> - npm run build` inside the code block. The list commands are not syntax-aware anywhere (they already mangle `- x` inside a fence), so this is a narrowing of accidental protection rather than a new class of bug — but the previously safe `>` case is a common one in notes that paste terminal output or quoted mail.

samples.summary: `shift()`'s new early `return` skips the `view.focus()` that `replacePrefixes` always performed.
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:343 `if (!top) return;` returns before `replacePrefixes`, which is the only place that calls `view.focus()` (list-commands.ts:278). Both call sites (`indentList` :353, `outdentList` :359) only enter `shift` with a non-zero step, which requires a marker line, so the path is unreachable today — but if either guard is ever relaxed the toolbar click would leave focus in the button instead of the editor, which is exactly what the `focus()` there exists to prevent.

samples.summary: The preview→source line mapping that `setTaskChecked` now trusts for quoted tasks is only exercised for a one-line document; no consumer test covers a quoted task item after preceding content.
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:260 maps a preview click to `setTaskChecked(view, line + 1, checked)` using the `TASK_LINE_ATTR` written from `list_item_open.map[0]` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:61-71). Previously a quoted item's click was a silent no-op (`check === null`), so a wrong map would have been harmless; now it rewrites a source line. The new test (`preview.test.ts:111`, doc `'> - [ ] quoted todo'`) asserts line 0 only, so the case where the quoted list follows other lines — the one where an off-by-one would flip a different task — is untested. markdown-it keeps absolute line numbers through `blockquote`, so this is likely fine; confirming needs a preview test with a quoted task on a later line asserting the same offset.
